newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Cohen denounces N.Korea's "dying" commmunist system.
newsitem.headline: Cohen denounces N.Korea's "dying" commmunist system.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen on Thursday denounced North Korea's "decaying and dying" communist system and called on Pyongyang to make peace with South Korea.

"They remain perhaps one of the few countries in the world today that still subscribe to a communist theology and economic system, which is decaying and dying," Cohen told reporters at the Demilitarised Zone, which has divided the two Koreas since the 1950-53 Korean War.
Cohen, winding up his first visit to the western Pacific and Asia, was asked by reporters if he had a message for the leadership of North Korea, where a critical food shortage has caused near-famine.

"If they can read my lips, I would hope that they would see the futility of putting up signs and trying to promote propaganda of a failed and failing system," he said as he stood in one of the world's most heavily-fortified areas.
The secretary was apparently being closely watched by North Korean border guards on the other side of the fence in the four-km (2.5 mile)-wide DMZ, which was set up when a truce ended the war.

He said he hoped North Korea would recognise "sooner rather than later", the benefits of South Korea's democracy. "But in the meantime, we have to remain ever vigilant...at a time when it seems to me that their economy and their entire system needs some relief from the burden that they have been carrying for too many years," he said.
